newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu takes battle for Jerusalem to street.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu takes battle for Jerusalem to street.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took his battle over Jerusalem to the streets on Monday, touring the occupied Arab half of the city while Palestinians shut down to protest Israeli building plans.

Netanyahu, trying to smother Arab anger at his plans to build 6,500 homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem, promised during a visit to the al-Thouri neighbourhood to upgrade infrastructure in the Arab half of the city.

"What we are doing today is making...Jerusalem one city for Jews and Arabs alike," he said at a site where Israel had unloaded materials for a sidewalk. "We are serious about it. It's not a ploy. We're not playing games."

Thouri, which straddles Jewish West Jerusalem, was shuttered like the rest of the West Bank and Gaza Strip by a general strike called to protest Israeli plans to build housing for Jews in Jerusalem's Jabal Abu Ghneim, also known as Har Homa.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said Palestinians had to accept the Har Homa decision, made by the government last week, and move on.

"Har Homa is a decision that stands on its own and it is very important that the Palestinians evaluate it correctly because we must progress in the negotiations even when there are disagreements," Mordechai told reporters in parliament.
"Certainly, certainly not use violence because violence does not serve anyone, it only drives to extremes and worsens the situation," he said.
If violence erupted "we will do what is called for", Mordechai warned.
Israel's moves in Jerusalem spurred violence in September. Sixty-one Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died in gunbattles after Netanyahu opened a tourist tunnel near Islamic holy shrines.
President Bill Clinton on Monday opened talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat by saying he regretted Israel's decision to build new housing for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.

"I would have preferred the decision not have been made because I don't think it builds confidence, I think it builds mistrust," Clinton told reporters at the start of his White House meeting with Arafat.
Israeli officials on Monday said Mordechai was pushing a plan to build 1,500 homes for Jews and 3,000 hotel rooms to link Maaleh Adumim settlement with Jewish enclaves north of the city.

Asked about the plan, Netanyahu said: "I haven't checked the bureaucratic procedures. But it's well known that we have plans to facilitate the development of Jerusalem for its Arab and Jewish residents alike."
The projects complete a circle of Jewish settlements around East Jerusalem which Israel began building after it captured the city in the 1967 Middle East war.
The Israeli moves came just weeks before Israel and the Palestinians are due to resume talks on a permanent peace deal, which are to include negotiations on the future of Jerusalem.

Israel captured East Jerusalem along with the West Bank and the Gaza Strip in the 1967 Middle East war. In a move not recognised internationally, it later annexed East Jerusalem, declaring it part of an indivisible capital. Palestinians want East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future state.
Arafat on Saturday accused Netanyahu of trying to destroy the peace process. He warned he might declare an independent Palestinian state in response to Netanyahu's moves.
Netanyahu responded by saying Arafat would bring peace moves to a halt if he unilaterally declared a state now.
